_meta: This file is guidance, not an official VAG fault-code catalog. VAG's internal 5-digit fault numbers (the kind VCDS prints, e.g. '01314 - Throttle Position Sensor') aren't something we can reliably recite from memory for every module/model-year combination, and getting one wrong is worse than not having it. Entries below have 'vag_fault_code': null until confirmed against a real capture from this car (see vagscan.vag bus logger) - fill it in once you've seen it on the wire, that's the intended workflow for growing this file over time.

title: Known Simos 7.1 access limits via ELM327
description: Simos 7.1 on this platform speaks VAG's KWP2000-over-CAN (TP20), not the plain ISO-TP the ELM327's built-in OBD modes use. Generic Mode 01/03/04/07/0A (vagscan.obd2) work over the emissions-related OBD-II part of this ECU regardless. Anything beyond that (full measuring blocks / adaptation channels / coding) goes through vagscan.vag's TP20 client, which is experimental and needs validation against this specific car before being trusted for anything beyond read-only use.
suggested_checks: Use the bus logger (vagscan.vag) with the car running and a scan tool like VCDS unavailable/available for comparison, to confirm TP20 channel IDs and timing before relying on write operations (DTC clear, adaptation).
source: engineering note, not a fault code

title: Seatbelt tensioner squib circuit fault
description: SRS module reports an open or short circuit in a seatbelt pretensioner's pyrotechnic squib loop, or its resistance is outside the expected range.
common_causes: Actually fired (deployed) tensioner from a prior collision
suggested_checks: Visually confirm the tensioner has not actually fired before assuming a wiring fault
Inspect and clean the under-seat connector
Never probe a squib circuit with a generic multimeter - its current can fire the pyrotechnic device; use a purpose-built airbag simulator/resistor substitute tool
source: general SRS diagnostic knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Side/curtain airbag squib circuit fault
description: SRS module reports an open or short circuit in a side or curtain airbag squib loop.
common_causes: Connector corrosion in the B-pillar/seat wiring
Wiring damage from upholstery work or a prior collision repair
suggested_checks: Confirm no prior deployment before clearing
source: general SRS diagnostic knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Occupant detection / seat mat fault
description: Passenger seat occupant classification sensor mat implausible or open circuit, affecting passenger airbag enable/disable logic.
common_causes: Sensor mat damaged by cleaning liquids or wear
Aftermarket seat cover pinching the mat
suggested_checks: Check for non-OEM seat covers compressing the mat
source: general SRS diagnostic knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Crash event data present (deployment history)
description: The SRS module has stored crash/deployment event data from an actual airbag deployment.
suggested_checks: Do not clear this without understanding it reflects an actual event - if buying a used car, this can indicate undisclosed prior airbag deployment/repair
source: general SRS diagnostic knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Immobilizer/cluster synchronization implausible
description: Cluster reports a mismatch talking to the immobilizer function (often integrated in the cluster on this platform generation).
common_causes: Battery disconnect/replacement without an adaptation procedure
Aftermarket alarm/remote-start wiring interfering with the ignition circuit
suggested_checks: Check for aftermarket alarm/immobilizer bypass wiring
This may require dealer-level security-access login to resolve - beyond generic ELM327 scope by design (immobilizer bypass is out of scope for this project)
source: general platform knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Lost communication with engine/ABS/airbag module (network)
description: Cluster reports it can't reach another module on the bus - cross-reference with a U0xxx generic code and check that module directly.
common_causes: The other module's own fault (check it directly)
Bus wiring/connector issue affecting that module specifically
suggested_checks: Check its fuse/power/ground and bus wiring
source: general platform knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Steering angle sensor implausible/not calibrated
description: ESP reports the steering angle sensor signal is missing or not calibrated.
common_causes: Battery disconnect or steering rack/column work without recalibration
suggested_checks: Perform steering angle sensor basic setting/calibration after any battery disconnect or steering work
source: general platform knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Brake light switch implausible
description: ESP reports the brake pedal switch signal doesn't match other inputs (e.g. brake pressure sensor).
common_causes: Misadjusted or failed brake light switch
Wiring fault at the pedal box
suggested_checks: Inspect wiring at the pedal box
source: general platform knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup

title: Central locking / window module communication fault
description: Comfort module reports a communication or actuator fault, commonly a door/window/lock module.
common_causes: Door wiring harness fatigue at the door-to-body boot (very common failure point)
suggested_checks: Inspect the wiring boot between each door and the body pillar for broken conductors
Check the specific door module reporting the fault
source: general platform knowledge, not a specific VAG code lookup
